taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-10, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 104.3 | 6.31 | 6.31
2 | 416.7 | 17.57 | 23.88
3 | 264.5 | 2.29 | 26.17
4 | 856.9 | 2.63 | 28.80
5 | 641.5 | 26.88 | 55.68
6 | 7698.1 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KHKH-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-10, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Note – Station T-10 (Survey Area T)**

The VES interpretation at T-10 resolves a six-layer resistivity sequence: a moderately resistive surface layer (104.3 Ω·m, 6.31 m thick) overlying a resistive layer (416.7 Ω·m, 17.57 m), followed by a lower-resistivity layer (264.5 Ω·m, 2.29 m), then a thin high-resistivity layer (856.9 Ω·m, 2.63 m), a layer of intermediate resistivity (641.5 Ω·m, 26.88 m), and a highly resistive basal layer (7698.1 Ω·m, inferred bedrock/substratum).

Applying the standard three-layer curve-type rules to each triplet of resistivities gives: layers 1-2-3 → K, 2-3-4 → H, 3-4-5 → K, 4-5-6 → H, yielding the composite curve type KHKH. This matches the classification on file. No discrepancy was found between the tabulated resistivity values and the stated curve type; the KHKH designation is confirmed as consistent with the layer model.

{"curve_type_stated": "KHKH", "label_issue_flagged": false}
